firestore.reasoning:
To fulfill the user's requirement of accessing all quiz responses, and adhering to the core design principles, particularly Authorization Independence and QAPs (Rules are not Filters), the proposed Firestore structure focuses on segregating data based on ownership and providing a membership model where appropriate. Given the prompt, there is an implied requirement to allow the main user to see responses given to a Quiz, this will be achieved by placing QuizResponses within a collection owned by the quiz creator. 

Quizzes are stored under `/quizzes/{quizId}`. Quiz questions related to a quiz are stored in a subcollection: `/quizzes/{quizId}/questions/{questionId}`. The quiz creator has full control over their quizzes and the associated questions.

Quiz responses for a specific quiz question will be stored within a subcollection: `/quizzes/{quizId}/questions/{questionId}/responses/{responseId}`. Because the responses are nested under the quiz question and quiz itself, the person that created the quiz will have access to read and write the responses. This approach allows the main user (the quiz creator) to view all responses to their quizzes without needing complex security rules or querying across different collections. The structure also supports list operations efficiently (QAPs) because the rules can simply check if the user has access to the quiz, and if so, they can list the associated questions and responses.

This structure promotes Authorization Independence by nesting the responses under the quiz. This makes authorization straightforward: the quiz creator implicitly has access to all responses under their quiz. This avoids the need for complex `get()` calls in the security rules to check ownership or membership.
